collection.description: There's a small, round lagoon on the east side of the island where the water is perfectly still, even in a storm.

ask.text:
There's a small, round lagoon on the east side of the island where the water is perfectly still, even in a storm. The fishers won't fish in it. They say the lagoon "keeps time," and that anyone who swims across it might be given some back, or have some taken.
(Name) has lost a bet, and the price is swimming across. (His/Her) friends are waiting on the far side, grinning. The water is so clear that (he/she) can see the white sand at the bottom, and something like a slow, glittering current going round in a circle.
Should (name) swim with the current or against it?

c1o1.text: (Name) climbs out on the far side and (his/her) friends stop grinning. (He/She) is ten years younger: the lines gone, the old aches gone, the knee that clicks has stopped clicking. "It gave me some back," (name) says, amazed. (His/Her) friends are already arguing about whose turn it is next. The elders put a stop to that by the afternoon.

c1o2.text: The current carries (him/her) round and round, and the swim takes much longer than it should. When (name) finally drags (himself/herself) out, (his/her) hair is grey at the temples and there are lines round (his/her) eyes that weren't there an hour ago. The lagoon has taken ten years for itself. "Well," says (name), after a long silence, "I won the bet back, at least." (He/She) didn't. Nobody has the heart to say so.

c1.text: (Name) slips in and lets the slow circle carry (him/her). It's warm, and easy, like being rocked. The far shore comes closer, then further, then closer...

c2o1.text: (Name) arrives exhausted, and lies on the sand gasping, and when (his/her) friends help (him/her) up, they keep staring at (his/her) face. Younger. Not (his/her) body, which aches as much as ever, just (his/her) face. "It took the time back from my face," (name) says, feeling (his/her) cheeks, "and put it all in my legs."

c2o2.text: (Name) fights across, and drags (himself/herself) out, and nothing has changed at all, except that (he/she) is very tired and very wet. "It didn't want my time," (he/she) says, sounding almost offended. (His/Her) friends pay for the next bet out of embarrassment for (him/her).

c2.text: (Name) kicks hard against the slow circle. It's like swimming through honey. Every stroke feels like an hour...
